recipes.name: Butternut Squash Fries
ingredients_raw: 1 (2 pound) butternut squash, halved and seeded

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
Use a sharp knife to carefully cut away the peel from the squash. Cut the squash into sticks, about 1/3 inch thick.
Blot any moisture from the butternut squash fries with paper towels, then arrange squash pieces on a baking sheet. Season with salt.
Bake in the preheated oven until brown and crisp on the edges, about 20 minutes, turning once.

raw_recipe.headline: Butternut Squash Fries
raw_recipe.description: These butternut squash fries are baked in the oven until browned and crisp for a tasty, low-carb alternative to regular fries or sweet potato fries.

review.reviewBody: I shook these in a gallon zip-loc bag with olive oil and kosher salt. I spread them evenly on baking sheets and flipped often. Occasionally the excess water from the squash would pool in the pans so I drained them once or twice during baking and I really think this helped cut down on the mushiness. They are softer than french fries, but mine were not really mushy. Delicious!! My kids liked these as well as the adults at my dinner tonight. I will make these again for sure.

I chose to cook these in my air fryer. I set the cut butternut squash fries on the grate at the bottom of the pan and cooked them for about 15 minutes or so at 400°. The key is to keep checking them because they do burn quickly because of the high sugar content in the vegetable. They turned out great, not soggy at all because the water was able to drain away under the grate. Very delicious and a great way to get another veggie into my diet. Those without an air fryer might want to set a cooling rack on the baking pan and arrange the "fries" on the rack so that the excess water can drain away under the vegetable as it cooks.

Not quite as good as sweet potato fries. I do not like that they do not crisp up easily, but they tasted pretty good. I used a baking rack in the oven with a sheet pan so the fries did not turn out soggy. That did help! I added a tablespoon of olive oil and sprinkled a small amount of sea salt and pepper on them. I think next time I want to try them with a small bit of brown sugar and cinnamon! I will definitely make these again!

I salted the raw cut-up squash, let sit, and soaked up excess moisture with paper towels. I shook squash in bag with some EVOO and then I spread out on cookie sheet and sprinkled it with cinnamon, allspice, garlic powder, cumin, and chili powder. I baked it for 45 minutes and it came out perfect and very tasty.

Love them!! If you like sweet potato fries, these are a great substitute. I cut them thinner with a crinkle cutter and spray with cooking oil. We use garlic salt after they are done cooking. They are not crispy but I find if you cut them thinner they aren't as mushy. FYI - if you are on Weight Watchers, these are no points if you use the cooking spray!!!

These were ok, but if I were to make them again I'd definitely add seasonings, oil and change the cook time. I found it odd that there was no fat, but I followed the recipe any way. After 20 minutes, they just looked soggy and undercooked with zero browning. I sprayed them with oil and put them back in for 5 mins. Still not done, but better. Another 5 minutes, then another 5, for a total of 35 minutes. Finally, some browning around the edges as promised, but not crispy at all like a fry. The oil is essential, as well as a longer cook time. I also recommend using parchment paper, as these will stick terribly to a sheet pan. Sweet potato fries are better.

I gave my butternut a quick 5/8 Min boil then I gave it a cold soak I then fried them in coconut oil. It came out delicious
Froze remainder butternut unfried
I treated like we do zuchini or eggplant. salt them and put them on a papertowel and let the salt pull water from them...then oil, season and bake. HUGE difference and more like fries.

After reading numerous reviews (positive and negative) I decided to slice the butternut squash thin, thick linguine noodle size strips. I stored the noodle like strips on a thick layer of paper towels in an air tight container overnight. Prior to placing them in the oven I sprayed the squash with butter cooking spray and then sprinkled the squash with garlic powder. 15 minutes in the oven the last 3-5 minutes under broil heat, Healthy, crispy and so delicious. WINNER!

This was a good basic recipe for fries. I salted before fries before hand on a paper towel to expell some of the water so fries would not be soggy. Let them rest about 10 min. Then I used some olive oil in the bottom of my baking dish and broiled them turning a few times for about 15-20 min and they were very good

First, read all reviews! I coated my slices in a mixture of olive oil, garlic salt and parsley to taste. Cooked at recommended temp for 15 minutes on the second to highest rack (pan was coated with foil). The fries were cooked, but not crispy. I turned my broiler on low for another 15 minutes, thus avoiding the need to turn them over as the tin foil crisped the underside. HUGE winner with me and my 4 year old twins ate them up without question or ketchup!
Hubby doesn't like squash, but loved these! Easy to make and delicious!!
I loved them
Seasoned with salt pepper and onion powder. Absolutely delicious!

I made them with krinkle precut butternut squash I bought from Trader Joes. So easy that way. Maybe next time I might tumble them in some olive oil first. I didn't add salt but better than what I expected. Thank you!

I have made it twice and will definitely make it again. The first time I used to much Cajun seasoning and it was too hot and salty. I toned it back some the second time and it was better. In both cases I found that 20 minutes was not enough cooking time. They did not look cooked and they were too hard and had to go back into the oven. I had to add another 15 minutes at least. But great recipe and wonderful to have guilt free fries!
Good recipe and I just added coconut oil to the pan on broil and they sizzled. Some came out pretty perfect and the rest were just really yummy.

Never tried doing this with squash before and it was TERRIFIC! Used a baggie with olive oil, garlic powder, cinnamon, curry, and salt. Baked for about 30 minutes without turning. Irresistible! Can't wait to make more -

Yummy! This is definitively something I will make again. I followed the suggestions in the comments of brushing with olive oil first then baking and then I sprinkled with some salt afterwards. I used a crookneck squash instead of butternut because that's the variety I have growing in my garden. I am sure any variety of squash would work.

Very yummy! I almost ate the whole squash! The only reason I gave it 4 out of 5 stars is due to texture and the amount of time this takes. I couldn't get mine crispy enough but I think if I had a double broiler that maybe would have solved the problem. I sprinkled my "fries" with salt and let the moisture sweat out onto napkins before baking. All in all I don't think I would make this again unless I am really craving it. I think I will simply roast them. Seems easier.
